sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Rain is normally brought through prayer, but Rashbi's Torah study had the quality of prayer, so he brought rain through Torah.

translations.translation: And the reason for this, that specifically Rashbi brought down rain through the utterance of Torah,
is,
that the descent of rain
(after there was initially a cessation of rain)
is a change in the world,
for that a change occurs in the world is
(generally)
through prayer,
as explained in Tanya18.
But in Rashbi,
even in his engagement with Torah there was
(also)
the quality of prayer,
and therefore he brought down rain through the utterance of Torah.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The difference between Torah and prayer is like the difference between blessing and prayer: prayer is from below to above, while blessing is from above to below.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that the distinction between Torah and prayer is analogous to the distinction between blessing and prayer19.
For prayer is from below to above
(as above),
that the one who prays is below and requests that they bestow upon him from above,
and blessing is from above to below,
that the one who blesses
[he who has the power to bless,
and in the manner of Avraham Avinu, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said "the blessings are given to you"20]
is above the root from which the blessing is drawn, and draws it from above to below.
And this is that blessing is in the manner of a command,
for the one who blesses is above the root from which the blessing is drawn, and therefore has the power to command.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Although blessing is superior regarding the person, prayer draws a new light from Ein Sof beyond the chain of descent, which is a higher form of drawing down.

translations.translation: Now, the superiority of blessing over prayer is with regard to the person who blesses and the person who prays,
but with regard to the drawing down itself,
the drawing down through prayer is more elevated.
For the matter of blessing is to draw down what already exists in the source, and not something new,
and the matter of prayer is a request from the Holy One, blessed be He, that even if the influence is not changed in the source, Heaven forbid,
and moreover, that it has been decreed upon him that he should be ill, Heaven forbid, or the like,
nevertheless,
a new influence shall be drawn to him from Ein Sof, which is above the chain of descent.
For this is what is said in several prayers: "May it be [His] will,"
for the explanation of "May it be [His] will" is that there should be a new will.
And the reason for this, that the drawing down of a new light is specifically through prayer,
is "for You desire the work of Your hands"21,
and therefore,
through prayer,
the service of the lower one,
they reach Ein Sof which is above the chain of descent.
